name: temp-file-sweeper
description: Report, relocate under .temp_files/, or delete stray top-level temporary files (.log, .txt, .tmp, .out, .err, .bak, .old) in a directory. Reporting is the default and changes nothing; move and delete act only on files git proves untracked in that exact work tree, are bounded by maxActions, and never touch a protected name.
guide:
# temp-file-sweeper

Finds stray temporary files accidentally created at the TOP LEVEL of a directory — build logs, `.txt` scratch notes, `.out`/`.err` dumps left behind by a command or by a post-commit step — and, on request, relocates them under `.temp_files/` or deletes them.

## Modes

- `report` (default): changes NOTHING; lists every matched file together with the git evidence for it. Safe to run anywhere, including the repository root.
- `move`: relocates matched files to `<quarantineDir>/<name>`, by default `.temp_files/swept/<name>`. A name collision inside the destination gains a `-1`, `-2` suffix.
- `delete`: unlinks matched files.

## Safety model

1. Only the top level of `root` is scanned. Subdirectories are never entered, so `.temp_files/` contents can never be re-swept.
2. `report` is the default, so omitting `mode` cannot destroy anything.
3. `move` and `delete` act only on files git proves untracked in that exact work tree (the work-tree root must be the swept root itself). Anything else lands in `skipped` with a reason, unless `includeTracked: true` accepts it explicitly.
4. Protected names (package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.json, README.md, AGENTS.md, LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md, .gitignore, kit.json, ...) are never swept.
5. `maxActions` bounds how many files a single call may touch (default 50).
6. `sinceMinutes` can narrow the sweep to recently written leftovers (0 disables the age filter).

## Parameters

| Name | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mode | report | report, move or delete |
| root | . | project-relative directory to sweep; a `@kit/...` value sweeps a disposable copy of a bundled fixture, while `@git/...` also makes that copy a throwaway git work tree and stages the names listed in the fixture `.staged` JSON array; either form also backdates the files named in an `.aged` JSON array to a fixed 2001 timestamp (all of this exists to serve the verification cases) |
| extensions | .log .txt .tmp .out .err .bak .old | extensions treated as temporary |
| sinceMinutes | 0 | only files modified within the last N minutes |
| maxActions | 50 | maximum files acted on in one call |
| includeTracked | false | act on files that lack untracked evidence |
| quarantineDir | .temp_files/swept | move destination, relative to the swept root |

## Result

`candidates` lists matched files that passed every filter, each with a `reason` of `untracked`, `tracked` or `tracked-state-unknown`. In `report` mode every match appears there. In `move`/`delete` mode only the files that will actually be acted on stay in `candidates`; the rest move to `skipped` (`tracked`, `tracked-state-unknown`, `protected-name`, `outside-time-window`, `max-actions-reached`). `gitWorkTree` is true only when the swept root itself resolved as a git work-tree root. All paths are relative to the swept root, and every list is sorted by path.

## Typical uses

- See what is lying around before committing: `{ "mode": "report", "root": ".", "sinceMinutes": 60 }`.
- Quarantine instead of losing it: run a report first, then `{ "mode": "move", "root": ".", "includeTracked": true }`.
- Clear it out for real: `{ "mode": "delete", "root": "." }`, relying on git to prove the files are untracked.

## Known limits

- Top level only: `node_modules/x.log` or `packages/a/tmp.txt` are out of scope by design.
- The verification cases cover all three evidence states: `@kit/...` yields `tracked-state-unknown`, `@git/...` on a fixture without `.staged` yields `untracked` (mutation allowed on real evidence), and `@git/...` with a `.staged` list yields `tracked` for exactly the staged names. The `@git/` cases need `git` on PATH, and the fixture pins `core.excludesFile` inside its own scratch so a developer global gitignore cannot change their outcome.
- `sinceMinutes` is covered in both directions: a fixture may name files in an `.aged` JSON array, which backdates them to a fixed 2001-01-01 timestamp before the sweep, so the `outside-time-window` branch has a deterministic case. Collision suffixes are individually cased up to `-3`; later ones follow the same suffix loop and have no case of their own.
- Deletion is irreversible; there is no undo. Prefer `move` when unsure.

inputSchema.description: Sweep parameters. Every field has a default, so an empty object is a safe report.

mode.description: report changes nothing, move relocates files under quarantineDir, delete unlinks them.

root.description: Project-relative directory to sweep. A @kit/<path> value sweeps a disposable copy of that bundled fixture instead; an @git/<path> value also makes that copy a throwaway git work tree and stages the names listed in the fixture .staged file.

extensions.description: File extensions treated as temporary. A leading dot is optional.

sinceMinutes.description: Only sweep files modified within the last N minutes; 0 disables the age filter.

maxActions.description: Maximum number of files one call may move or delete.

includeTracked.description: Act on files that are not proven untracked (tracked, or no git work tree). Required for a mutation inside a directory that is not its own git work-tree root.

quarantineDir.description: Move destination, relative to the swept root. Must be a plain relative path.

outputSchema.description: Sweep result. Every path is relative to the swept root.

root.description: The root exactly as it was requested.

gitWorkTree.description: True only when the swept root itself is a git work-tree root, so untracked evidence is real.

scanned.description: Top-level regular files examined, before the extension filter.

candidates.description: Matched files that passed every filter, sorted by path.

skipped.description: Matched files that were not acted on, sorted by path.

tests.name: report is the default and changes nothing
move refuses files without untracked evidence
move relocates matched files under the quarantine directory
delete honours the protected-name list under a narrowed extension filter
a positive time window still accepts freshly written files
maxActions bounds how many files one call may act on
git work tree: a staged file is tracked and skipped while an untracked one still moves
git work tree: genuinely untracked files need no includeTracked override
quarantine name collision gains a -1 suffix instead of overwriting
a second name collision in the same destination gains a -2 suffix
sinceMinutes excludes an older file from the sweep but keeps the fresh one
a third name collision in the same destination gains a -3 suffix
